name: Chisel
text: Adopt auto-publishing the full dissent log alongside the neutral third-party summary, tagged by resolution status (open/addressed/unresolved). This forces every team to confront *all* objections—not just the polished ones—while avoiding the spectacle risk of unfiltered raw dissent. The trade-off is that stakeholders must now parse more data, but the alternative—burying gaps behind severity labels or volume—creates worse blind spots.

name: Sift
text: The real risk is that publishing the full dissent log with resolution tags still lets leads bury unresolved objections in a sea of noise—stakeholders won’t dig past the first page, and unresolved items get lost in the volume. Better: auto-publish only the unresolved objections, but *group them by theme* (e.g., "safety," "creative integrity") and require a one-sentence explanation for why each remains unresolved. That forces clarity without drowning in raw data. Settle when the dissent log’s unresolved section is structured this way and the first draft exists.
